Laizuva Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšiai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Laizuva's Jewish community, settled in the second half of the 18th century, buried its dead in the neighboring town of Viekšniai for its first hundred years, until a local cemetery was established around 1860. Some families grew wealthy in the late-19th-century pig bristle trade, processed nearby and marketed in Courland, while many of their children emigrated to South Africa, the United States, and England. By 1941, only about 50 Jews remained in Laizuva; all were murdered that August at the Jewish cemetery in Mažeikiai, alongside the Jews of that entire district.
